title: if I had known ... / I wish I had known ...
subtitle: if I had known / I wish I had known
summary: Use if + had done and would have done to imagine a different past, and wish + had done to say you regret something that happened.

lesson.heading: Study this situation
lesson.text: Last month Gary was in hospital for a few days. Rachel didn't know this. A few days ago they met by chance, and Rachel said she would have visited him. If I'd known = If I had known. This tells us that she didn't know before.

examples.text: **If I'd known** you were in hospital, I **would have gone** to visit you.
examples.note: = I didn't know, so I didn't go to visit you

lesson.heading: if + had done ... for the past
lesson.text: We use **if + had ('d)** ... to talk about the past (if I'd known / if you'd done etc.). In the other part we use **would have** + past participle.

examples.text: I didn't see you when you passed me in the street. **If I'd seen** you, I **would have said** hello.
They didn't go out last night. They **would have gone** out **if they hadn't been** so tired.
**If you'd been looking** where you were going, you **wouldn't have walked** into the wall.
The view was wonderful. I **would have taken** some pictures **if I'd had** a camera with me.
examples.note: if I'd had = if I had had; but I didn't have a camera

left.label: now: if I was ... I would ...
examples: I'm not hungry. **If I was** hungry, I **would eat** something.

right.label: past: if I had been ... I would have ...
examples: I wasn't hungry. **If I had been** hungry, I **would have eaten** something.

lesson.heading: No would have in the if-part
lesson.text: We do not say 'if something would have happened'. We use **would** in the other part of the sentence. Be careful: the short form **'d** can be would or had.

examples.text: **If I had seen** you, I would have said hello.
examples.wrong: If I would have seen you

examples.note: I'd have said = I would have said

lesson.heading: wish + had done
lesson.text: We use had done/known/been etc. in the same way after **wish**. I wish something **had happened** = I am sorry that it didn't happen. I wish something **hadn't happened** = I am sorry that it happened. We do not say 'wish ... would have'.

examples.text: **I wish I'd known** that Gary was ill. I would have gone to see him.
I feel sick. **I wish I hadn't eaten** so much.
Do you **wish you'd studied** science instead of languages?
The weather was cold. **I wish it had been** warmer.
examples.wrong: I wish it would have been

lesson.note: Compare: I'm glad I saw him (= I saw him) and I wish I'd seen him (= I didn't see him).

left.label: would do (present result)
examples: If I'd gone to the party last night, **I would be** tired now. (I am not tired now - present)

right.label: would have done (past result)
examples: If I'd gone to the party last night, **I would have met** lots of people. (I didn't meet lots of people - past)

lesson.heading: would have, could have and might have
lesson.text: After if + had done, you can also use **could have** (= would have been able to) and **might have** (= maybe would have).

examples.text: If the weather hadn't been so bad, we **would have gone** out.
If the weather hadn't been so bad, we **could have gone** out.
examples.note: = we would have been able to go out

examples.text: If the weather hadn't been so bad, we **might have gone** out.
examples.note: = maybe we would have gone out

lesson.text: Talking about a past that didn't happen? Use had done in the if-part and would have done in the other part - never would have in both.

exercises.prompt: Rachel didn't know Gary was in hospital. She says: If I'd known you were in hospital, I ___ to visit you.
exercises.explanation: A past situation that didn't happen: if + had known, and would have gone in the other part.

exercises.prompt: Thanks for reminding me about Lisa's birthday. ___ if you hadn't reminded me.
exercises.explanation: The if-part is past (hadn't reminded), so the result uses would have: I'd have forgotten.

exercises.prompt: Sarah got to the station just in time to catch her train to the airport. If ___ the train, she would have missed her flight too.
exercises.explanation: Imagining a different past: if + had done (if she'd missed the train).

exercises.statement: If I would have seen you, I would have said hello.
exercises.explanation: If I had seen you, I would have said hello. We don't use would have in the if-part.

exercises.prompt: Their trip was OK, but they would have enjoyed it more if the weather ___ better.
exercises.explanation: Past situation: the if-part takes had + past participle (had been).

exercises.prompt: The accident happened because the road was icy. Write a sentence beginning If ...
exercises.answer: If the road hadn't been icy, the accident wouldn't have happened.
exercises.explanation: If + hadn't been (past) and wouldn't have happened in the other part.

exercises.prompt: You've painted the gate red. Now you think red was the wrong colour. You say: I wish ___ it red.
exercises.explanation: I wish something hadn't happened = I am sorry that it happened: I wish I hadn't painted it red.

exercises.prompt: I wasn't tired last night. If I ___ tired, I would have gone home earlier.
exercises.explanation: Last night is past, so the if-part needs had been (not was, which is for now).

exercises.prompt: Is the speaker imagining something about now, or about the past?

items.text: If I was hungry, I would eat something.
If I had been hungry, I would have eaten something.
If I'd gone to the party, I would be tired now.
If I'd gone to the party, I would have met lots of people.
I wish I hadn't eaten so much.
I wish I knew his phone number.

exercises.statement: If I'd gone to the party last night, I would be tired now.
exercises.explanation: Correct. The if-part is past (I'd gone), but the result is about now, so would be is right.

exercises.prompt: You didn't have any breakfast - that's why you're hungry now. Write a sentence beginning If ...
exercises.answer: If you'd had some breakfast, you wouldn't be hungry now.
exercises.explanation: The if-part is past (you'd had), but the result is present (now), so wouldn't be.

exercises.prompt: You decided to travel by car, but the journey was long and tiring. Going by train would have been better. You say: I wish ___ by train.
exercises.explanation: A regret about the past: wish + had done (I wish we'd gone by train).
